extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word when exposed to the whole passage but not when only seeing the last sentence. It is designed to evaluate computational models' ability to understand broad discourse context through a word prediction task.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages were extracted from the BookCorpus (unpublished novels), filtered for offensive material and duplicates, then filtered using language models to remove easy examples. Remaining passages were evaluated by human subjects via CrowdFlower crowdsourcing in three steps.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The BookCorpus, containing 5,325 novels and 465 million words (after duplicate removal and filtering), consisting of unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-step crowdsourcing pipeline: (1) one subject guesses target word from whole passage; if correct, (2) a second subject guesses from whole passage; if correct, (3) up to 10 subjects try to guess from target sentence only (3 guesses each); passage included in dataset only if no subject in step 3 guesses correctly. Subjects could not judge the same item in both passage and sentence conditions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 84–86% of items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2, and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about 1 in 25 input examples passed all selection steps. Average cost per item was $1.24.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 annotators for passage condition (steps 1 and 2); up to 10 annotators for sentence-only condition (step 3)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is derived from unpublished novels in the BookCorpus, which minimizes usefulness of general world knowledge and external resources. Potentially offensive material was filtered out using a stop word list. The dataset is designed so that models should be trained on raw text from the training partition, limiting its use for other training scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating language understanding in NLP models, specifically testing whether models can predict the last word of a target sentence given a broader discourse context. Models tackling LAMBADA should be trained on raw text from the training partition.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Passages easy for standard language models were filtered out (target word probability ≥0.00175 by any of four language models excluded). Novels were randomly divided into equally-sized training and development+testing partitions, with further splitting of LAMBADA data between development and testing.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material using a stop word list were applied to the Book Corpus. Context size was defined as the minimum number of complete sentences containing at least 50 tokens before the target sentence. The target word is constrained to be the last word of the target sentence.

name.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task.

description.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
